claim: On Portals our queen steps through a portal into a small pearl room by round 5 in every game and dies in a room of 6 tiles or fewer in 9 of 9 main and 26 of 27 v31 games; their queen takes a portal step in 2 of 9 and 12 of 27 games and is alive at the end in 4 of 9 and 6 of 27.
how_to_count: Games with map_key Portals #1, our_code main and v31 separately. Room of a tile = the set of tiles joined to it by edges that are neither kelp nor portal (the board wrap is an ordinary edge). For each queen (lowest starting dragon id of a side): room size of her head tile at her dragonDeath event; number of head moves across a portal edge before death; the first raw round in which one of her turns starts with her head in a room of 6 tiles or fewer; cause of death (engine reason; for reason 2 the side of the body she hit); alive at the end. Also count how many of her turn starts are in rooms of 6 or fewer.

claim: On layouts where the queen can leave spawn, the share of games in which our queen dies as the standing victim of an enemy head-on rises with opponent rating in both codes, and against teams rated 2100 or more our queen is almost never alive at the end.
how_to_count: rows.jsonl, map queen_spawn_dead_end false, our_code main and v31 separately, bands by opponent_rating: 1700-1899, 1900-2099, 2100+. Our queen rammed = queen.us.death_cause is head-on and queen.us.head_on.victim equals queen.us.id. Their queen rammed = the same on queen.them. Alive at the end = queen.*.alive_end. Please also check whether one opponent or one layout carries the 2100+ cells and give a chance figure for the trend.

claim: The gap in heads standing within 2 tiles of a busy tile (theirs minus ours, snapshots with dragon counts within 10 percent, layouts with 1500 or more open tiles) is about the same size against every opponent rating band and is already present at rounds 50 and 75. Per game, a bigger gap goes with a smaller share of pearls for us in r101-300 on Around UNSW and on Slithery Fight.
how_to_count: As the F20 entry of the 04:00 queue (busy tile = 8 or more natural pearl births in that game; head within 2 tiles wrapped Manhattan; snapshot at the start of the raw round; kept when both sides have dragons and each count is at most 1.1 times the other). Two additions: split the r100-300 snapshots (every 25 rounds) by opponent_rating band; and take snapshots at the start of raw rounds 50 and 75, pooled. Cost: for each main or v31 game on Around UNSW #1 and on Slithery Fight #1 with at least 3 kept snapshots in r100-300, gap = pooled their share minus pooled our share over the kept snapshots; pearl share = pearls r101-300 our_share from rows.jsonl; Spearman rank correlation per layout, main and v31 together and apart.

claim: When our lone queen is rammed on main, a legal single step that ends beyond the full reach of every nearby enemy head existed in only 5 of 28 rams (33 of 75 on v31), so her own last step could rarely have saved her.
how_to_count: Population as the F13 entry of the 04:00 queue: free layouts, cross-team head-on in which our queen is the standing victim and their queen is already dead, rams where the rammer was alive at the start of her last own turn before the ram. Board at the start of that turn. Enemy heads considered = those within 6 tiles (wrapped Manhattan) of her head, plus the rammer. Full reach of a dragon of length L = ceil(L/4) + L - 2; free reach = ceil(L/4). A step is legal when its edge is not kelp and the target tile holds no dragon body at that moment (portal steps count). A step is safe when the path distance (kelp and portals respected, dragons ignored) from every such enemy head to the target is greater than that head reach. Count rams with at least one safe step, for full reach and for free reach; the same for their lone queen.
